svg.title: GPU nesting: chip, SM, warp, thread
svg.desc: A nested-box diagram (not a tree) showing an H100 chip containing 132 streaming multiprocessors, each SM containing many warps of 32 threads running in lockstep, each warp containing individual threads. Each ring between boxes lists what that level owns: the chip owns HBM and the SM array, the SM owns shared memory, the warp scheduler, and tensor cores, the warp owns lockstep instruction issue, and the thread owns its own registers.

text.font-family: Iowan Old Style, Palatino, Georgia, serif

svg.text: Nested, not hierarchical: chip → SM → warp → thread

text.font-family: Iowan Old Style, Palatino, Georgia, serif

svg.text: H100 chip — 132 SMs, one shared 80 GB HBM pool

text.font-family: Iowan Old Style, Palatino, Georgia, serif

svg.text: chip owns: HBM (80 GB @ 3.35 TB/s), the 132-SM array, L2 cache (~50 MB)

text.font-family: Iowan Old Style, Palatino, Georgia, serif
Iowan Old Style, Palatino, Georgia, serif

svg.text: SM owns: shared memory / L1 (256 KB), the warp scheduler(s), tensor cores

text.font-family: Iowan Old Style, Palatino, Georgia, serif
Iowan Old Style, Palatino, Georgia, serif

svg.text: warp owns: one instruction issued to all 32 lanes per cycle
